status: registered before running any counterfactual tests
questions: Do released evolutionary edits have sufficient parent, child and outcome provenance for component-wise counterfactual evaluation?
In a chronological sample of real upstream harness changes, are multiple component edits necessary to pass the upstream regression tests?
Does an outcome-blind dependency-based scope selector improve on fixed grouping after counting scope size?

evidence_tiers.A: Solver task outcomes under parent, single-component and joint variants, using the same tasks and model budget.
evidence_tiers.B: Unmodified upstream regression tests executed on component subsets of real upstream commits. This measures maintenance correctness, NOT solver benchmark improvement or RSI.
evidence_tiers.C: Static dependencies, patch co-occurrence and published aggregate scores. These do NOT establish causal necessity.

dgm_sample.source: Official DGM README linked public swe_results.zip
dgm_sample.selection: First 40 timestamp-sorted candidate directories in swe_dgm with metadata.json. Keep failures and missing patches. Do not use ablation run directories as additional independent samples.
dgm_sample.counterfactual_limit: A candidate beating its parent does not establish necessity of its component combination. Such a claim needs subset executions; otherwise report only co-editing and observed parent/child scores.

upstream_regression_sample.head: 04d809ceab9df28f9adaed044884180159172930
upstream_regression_sample.order: first-parent history, newest first, maximum 120 commits inspected
upstream_regression_sample.include: Non-merge commits with semantic changes to src/minisweagent Python code and changes to upstream Python tests. Select before observing test outcomes.
upstream_regression_sample.exclude: Pure documentation, formatting, packaging/version-only changes; record reasons. No exclusion based on success, component count or observed interaction.
upstream_regression_sample.evaluation: All changed upstream test files, identical child-version tests for every production-code subset; report test collection/import errors separately.
upstream_regression_sample.component_rule: Fixed existing source directory boundaries: agents, models, environments, run, config, utils, core. No splitting modules to manufacture interactions.
upstream_regression_sample.matrix: Exhaust all changed-component subsets if k <= 4. For k > 4 record unsupported matrix instead of selective testing.
upstream_regression_sample.host_tests: Only after source review for dangerous external actions; no network/model credentials in test processes, isolated source copy and local temp HOME.

scope_arms.single: Smallest singleton covering the primary changed component, seed identified by largest AST-level source change (path tie break).
scope_arms.fixed: Predeclared groups: runtime={agents,models,environments,core}; support={run,config,utils}. Select the group containing the same primary component.
scope_arms.adaptive_static: Outcome-blind direct production dependency closure on the same primary component, considering imports and explicit class/protocol references; source-only, no test outcomes, no tuned grouping.
scope_arms.oracle: All changed production components, upper bound only; not a deployable selection policy.

limits.large_archive_access: range reads only unless whole archive is under limit

interpretation: A multi-file or multi-component patch is not evidence that its changes are all needed.
Subset import incompatibility is recorded separately from behavioral synergy.
If fixed grouping passes the same cases as adaptive grouping, no claim of adaptive correctness benefit is permitted.
A deterministic dependency heuristic is not a trained organization agent.
Do not report regression-test replay as a completed live improver or solver-task comparison.
Keep negative, unsupported, environment-failed, and no-op cases in the ledger.
